name: ArtifactsBench
description: ArtifactsBench is a benchmark and automated, multimodal evaluation paradigm for visual code generation. It comprises 1,825 diverse executable tasks across nine domains (Game Development, SVG Generation, Web Applications, Simulations, Data Science, Management Systems, Multimedia Editing, Quick Tools, and Others), stratified into Easy/Medium/Hard tiers. The framework renders each artifact and captures its dynamic behavior via temporal (three-step) screenshots, assessed by a Multimodal LLM (MLLM)-as-Judge guided by fine-grained, per-task checklists. It evaluates over 30 leading LLMs and achieves 94.4% ranking consistency with WebDev Arena.
creator: Tencent Hunyuan Team
citeAs: Tencent Hunyuan Team. ArtifactsBench: Bridging the Visual-Interactive Gap in LLM Code Generation Evaluation.
rai:dataCollection: Tasks were aggregated from expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query generation from screenshots. Automated filters dropped incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items, prioritizing dynamics (state changes, animations, responsiveness). Experts rewrote prompts for clarity, completeness, and executability; LLM rewriting added diverse styles; humans verified. Difficulty was assigned post hoc by aggregated performance of 30+ models.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, Software Collection, Secondary Data analysis
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Candidates were aggregated from expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query generation from screenshots.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Two-stage de-duplication and contamination control: (i) MinHash + semantic similarity over prompts, checklists, and normalized DOM/CSS/JS; (ii) screenshot perceptual hashing to catch visually near-identical artifacts. Flagged items were re-authored or discarded. Difficulty calibration was performed post hoc by aggregated performance of 30+ models to enforce 30%/40%/30% split.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Automated filters dropped incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items. Experts rewrote prompts for clarity, completeness, and executability. LLM rewriting added diverse styles with human verification. Solvability validation collected candidate solutions from multiple model families and pruned underspecified items. Tasks solved only by brittle hacks were revised or removed. Sub-categories were tagged by a lightweight classifier with human spot-checks.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each query was paired with a 10-dimension checklist covering visual, interactional, and code qualities. Checklists were LLM-drafted (by Hunyuan-Turbos) and then human-refined for specificity and screenability. A 10% manually curated seed anchored calibration and achieved Cohen's kappa >= 0.8 among annotators; the seed was reused as few-shot references. The 10 items are grouped into five vision-oriented and five code-oriented dimensions. For human validation, 280 queries with data from 6 models were independently scored by multiple front-end engineers in a double-blind protocol with randomized sample order; final human ground-truth score represents the median of individual annotators' ratings.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Cohen's kappa >= 0.8 was achieved among annotators for checklist calibration. Pairwise consistency rate (Pair ACC) was used to quantify agreement between automated referee and human experts. Agreement between Gemini-2.5-Pro referee and human experts reached up to 90.95% pairwise agreement. Cross-judge ranking consistency was compared between Gemini-2.5-Pro-Preview-0506 and Qwen2.5-VL-72B, showing largely consistent partial-order constraints with residual differences concentrated among top-tier systems.
rai:annotationsPerItem: 10 checklist dimensions per query (5 vision-oriented and 5 code-oriented)
rai:annotatorDemographics: Multiple engineers with extensive front-end development experience
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Hunyuan-Turbos (checklist generation), Gemini-2.5-Pro (referee scoring and query classification), Qwen2.5-VL-72B (referee scoring), Playwright/headless Chromium (artifact execution and screenshot capture at 1024x768 resolution)
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The benchmark, evaluation harness, and baseline results are open-sourced at https://artifactsbenchmark.github.io. Dataset specs, checklist templates, evaluation scripts, and referee settings are released. Future work targets richer dynamics beyond discrete screenshots, agentic multi-turn self-debugging, and broader artifact domains.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Queries are filtered to avoid requesting or involving any sensitive personal information such as phone numbers, addresses, or other identifiable details (Privacy dimension scored in quality filtering).
rai:dataSocialImpact: ArtifactsBench provides a scalable and accurate tool to accelerate the development of user-centric generative models. By enabling holistic, automated evaluation of interactive visual artifacts, it supports progress in LLM capabilities for real-world software creation including responsive web interfaces, data visualizations, and mini-games.
rai:dataBiases: The benchmark may not fully capture the fluidity, correctness, and robustness of highly complex, long-horizon, or state-dependent interactions via discrete screenshot sampling. Minor discrepancies are observed in fine-grained scoring of certain complex interactive tasks between different MLLM referees, reflecting potential cognitive biases in how different MLLMs interpret long-horizon interaction logic and dynamic visual feedback.
rai:dataLimitations: Current methodology evaluates dynamic behavior by capturing screenshots at fixed intervals, which may not fully capture complex, long-horizon, or state-dependent interactions. The benchmark focuses on single-turn artifact generation and does not assess agentic or iterative development capabilities. Even the best models struggle to surpass 50 points on the hardest subset. The evaluation does not cover video-based analysis of entire user sessions or programmatic DOM interaction for state verification.
rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluation of LLMs on interactive visual code generation tasks. The benchmark supports fine-grained capability analysis across nine domains and three difficulty tiers, diagnostic insights into model strengths and failure modes, and ranking of LLMs in alignment with human preferences for visual quality.
